meta.name: Plan benefit design, setup, and testing issues
meta.source_document: Sanford Issue Case Analysis- SN Trends-POC 1.2- Pharos Promptbook

focus: Recurring plan benefit design, setup, and testing issues: what failed, why it was not caught, which part of the organisation most likely contributed, and which systemic actions would prevent recurrence.

scope.instruction: Decide whether the case is relevant to plan benefit design, setup, and testing analysis. Classify even when evidence is incomplete and lower confidence instead of refusing.
in_scope: Plan benefit design or setup (configuration, coding, build, renewal, amendment)
Benefit rules (PA, step therapy, quantity limits)
Testing and validation of benefit design (BAT, UAT, pre-go-live validation)
Post-go-live issues that directly reveal a benefit design, setup, or testing failure
out_of_scope: Claims operations unless the claim issue directly reveals a benefit configuration error
Network, pricing, reimbursement, or finance issues not tied to benefit design
Workflow, intake, routing, or operational delays
Data feeds, file transfers, reporting issues
External vendor or pharmacy behavior not caused by benefit configuration

lens.name: category
lens.label: Category
lens.definition: The benefit area the failure belongs to. Pick up to two; use Unclassified when none fits.

lens.name: causal_class
lens.label: Causal class
lens.definition: Whether the failure most likely came from misunderstanding the client's intent, a coding or configuration error, or a testing and validation failure. Several can apply; use Indeterminate when the evidence cannot distinguish.

lens.name: owner
lens.label: Owner
lens.definition: Which part of the organisation most likely contributed: people (knowledge, judgement, communication), process (missing or skipped steps), or technology (system limits or defects). Use Indeterminate when the evidence does not say.

grouping.instruction: Group the cases into recurring themes. Every in-scope case must belong to at least one theme; a case may belong to more than one only when it clearly shows two distinct failure patterns. Prefer themes that share a failure mechanism over themes that only share a category.

report_template.title: Plan Benefit Design, Setup, and Testing Issue Analysis

sections.heading: 1. Executive wrapper
sections.text: Scope: plan benefit design, setup, and testing issues for {client}. Volume: {selected_count} cases opened {date_from} to {date_to} were reviewed; {in_scope_count} were classified in scope and analysed. ServiceNow data through {data_through}. {theme_count} themes identified.

sections.heading: Executive summary
sections.instruction: Write two short paragraphs for an executive reader: the main recurring themes and the systemic actions that matter most. Describe causes as likely contributing factors. Use only the theme data provided.

sections.heading: 2. Theme summary
sections.text: Grouped by category, then owner. Frequency is the share of in-scope cases.

sections.heading: 3. Introduction
sections.text: This analysis reviewed {selected_count} {client} cases and classified {in_scope_count} as plan benefit design, setup, or testing issues. Each in-scope case was analysed for what happened, what failed, where, how it was detected, what likely caused it, and what would prevent it, using ServiceNow case, task, and subtask text and linked attachments. Counts and timing are computed from the case records; causes and actions are candidate findings for review.

sections.heading: 5. Operational context (evidence queries)
sections.text: Answers below come from read-only queries over the ServiceNow evidence, generated by Genie and checked before use. Each shows its question and SQL.

questions.label: Task volume by assignment group
questions.question: For client_account {client_sql}, considering only cases opened between {date_from} and {date_to}, how many tasks did each task assignment group handle? Return task_assignment_group and task_count, highest first.

questions.label: Attachment coverage by case
questions.question: For client_account {client_sql}, for cases opened between {date_from} and {date_to}, list each case_number with the number of validated attachment files and how many of them have processing_status EXTRACTED. Include cases with no attachments.

sections.heading: Appendix A. Scope decisions to confirm
sections.text: Cases classified as out of scope (model classification; excluded from the themes).

sections.heading: Completion statement
sections.text: Theme consolidation complete: {theme_count} themes from {in_scope_count} in-scope of {selected_count} selected cases. All findings remain candidates pending reviewer validation.

style.tone: Plain, executive-friendly language. Describe causes as likely contributing factors, not established facts.
